headline: Six nested styled wrappers is the depth weak spot, and 9.7.0's headline gain: the perf runtime collapses the six-`Yak` chain to one, taking the styled lane from the 9.6.0 build's 5.12 ms/1k to 0.656 ms/1k — a 7.8× jump — while the css-prop fold merges all six classes into one and ties `vanilla`.

microbench.why: This is composition's worst case and the clearest read on the 9.7.0 runtime. The css-prop fold concatenates all six levels into one class and ties `vanilla` at 0.518 ms/1k. The styled lane cannot fold a six-deep `styled(...)` chain, but its perf runtime merges every level's attrs at construction and renders one wrapper — 0.656 ms/1k. The 9.6.0 styled build, which renders all six `Yak` bodies per element, sits at 5.12 ms/1k, so the perf runtime is a 7.8× gain on exactly the depth pattern real trees hit. The hash libraries scale with depth too (`styled-components` 1.48 ms/1k, `panda` 18.1 ms/1k).

autocannon.why: Under load the css-prop fold ties `vanilla` at ~1500 req/s; the perf-collapsed styled lane serves 1259, and the 9.6.0 build — six `Yak` bodies per request — manages only 190 req/s, a 6.6× gap the runtime closes.

attribution.why: The css-prop fold's library slice is 0.083 ms — six levels in one class — tying `vanilla`. The styled lane's 0.175 ms lib is the single perf-collapsed wrapper; the 9.6.0 build spends 4.17 ms of a 5.29 ms render in lib, six `Yak` bodies deep — the exact cost the perf runtime removes. `panda`'s css-fn reaches 18.2 ms of component self-time.

hydrate.why: The 9.7.0 lanes hydrate as pure JS at ~45 ms; the 9.6.0 build's six-wrapper tree hydrates in 66.7 ms, and the runtime libraries reflow their injected sheet to 101 ms (`styled-components`) and 117 ms (`panda`).

inp.why: A single six-deep update is ~7-8 ms for the 9.7.0 and static-class lanes within the interaction spread. The depth cost shows in the laggards: the 9.6.0 build re-renders six `Yak` bodies at 22.5 ms, `goober` 20.8 ms, `panda` 62.5 ms.

mount.why: The 9.7.0 lanes mount at ~68-70 ms; the 9.6.0 build's deeper tree mounts in 94.6 ms and the runtime libraries add first-inject (`styled-components` 98.3 ms, `panda` 144 ms).

renderTiming.why: One style recalc for every approach — parity; the styleMs spread is sub-millisecond.

payload.why: The css-prop fold collapses six levels into one class and ships smallest (2.66 kB gz); the styled lane carries the six-wrapper chain (4.04 kB); the runtime and utility lanes are 3.4-4.1× larger (`styled-components` 16.6 kB).

nsweep.why: At 4000 six-deep elements the css-prop fold and `vanilla` stay flat (~2.1 ms), the perf-collapsed styled lane 2.61 ms; the 9.6.0 build compounds six `Yak` bodies to 20.9 ms — an 8× curve the perf runtime flattens.

crossCase: `compose-6` is the deep end of the `compose-1`/`compose-3` sweep and where the release gain is largest: the styled lane's 9.6.0→9.7.0 speedup grows with depth (about 2.1× flat, 3.6× at depth 3, 7.8× here) because the perf runtime removes the `Yak → Yak` recursion that multiplied the runtime by depth. The css-prop fold sidesteps depth entirely by merging every level into one class.
